headline: South Asia: UNDERSTANDING THE NEW AGE OF WAR
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: UNDERSTANDING THE NEW AGE OF WAR.
- Africa: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
- India: Houthis' Saudi Airport Attacks Pressure Trump To Boost US Role In Yemen.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: 3 US soldiers awarded Purple Hearts after March missile attack on Saudi Arabia base.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: 3 US soldiers awarded Purple Hearts after March missile attack on Saudi Arabia base.
Sgt. Xavier Jones, SSgt. Kalob Mitchell and Spc. Nicholas Cabo were awarded Purple Hearts after a missile attack on Prince Sultan Air Base, Saudi Arabia.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Powerus unveils fully autonomous drone interceptors.
Once a threat is detected, the new Guardian 3 interceptors are immediately launched toward it. They strike using advanced AI and navigational systems.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: US Army creates robotics technician job to focus on drone warfare.
As experts in autonomous warfare, U.S. Army robotics technicians will advise commanders on how best to deploy autonomous systems during operations.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Constable Joel Robinson named top cop.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Constable Joel Robinson named top cop.
Constable Joel Robinson of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) St Catherine North Division walked away with the Chairman’s Award in the the 2026 LASCO, JCF Saluting Our Heroes Awards. Robinson, a school resource officer in the JCF’s Community Safety and Security Unit, emerged from a field of six finalists recognised for their contributions to policing and public service. His achievement also earned him a promotion to corporal, announced by Commissioner of Police Dr Kevin Blake.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Jamaica’s tourism stature reinforced on world stage.
WESTERN BUREAU: World Travel Awards founder and president Graham Cooke has hailed Jamaica’s international tourism standing, noting that the island’s selection to host the Caribbean and Americas awards ceremony reinforces its position among the world’s leading destinations.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Southern Europe - bottom line: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 21 hours ago: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
The strategy draws on lessons from Ukraine, putting cheap drones, AI and rapid military strikes at the heart of NATO's response to any Russian attack.
- Balkan Insight, Ukrainska Pravda, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Bulgaria Summons Russian Envoy Over New Black Sea Drone Attacks.
PM Rumen Radev summons Russian ambassador over latest drone strikes targeting ships in Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone, admitting Moscow likely 'benefited' from the attacks.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: The Ceuta fears shaping Spain’s election.
As the United States looks towards Russia for diesel, European leaders are doubling down on their support for Ukraine. On the show, hosts Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart unpack all the ways the EU plans to put its money where its mouth is and help Kyiv. Expect it to be the talk of the town […]

Der überraschende Rücktritt erschüttert die Koalition: SPD-Arbeitsministerin Bärbel Bas gibt ihren Rückzug von allen Ämtern bekannt. Ausgerechnet kurz vor dem wichtigen Arbeitgebertag heute. POLITICO-Chefkorrespondent Rasmus Buchsteiner ordnet zusammen mit Maximilian Stascheit ein, wie diese Personalie das zerrüttete Regierungsbündnis belastet und warum mit der eiligen Ernennung von Alexander Schweitzer die Proporzregeln der SPD über Bord geworfen […]
Western Russia - bottom line: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks.
- The Moscow Times, one day ago: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks.

- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Zelenskyy: No warning from partners about Russian ballistic strike on Kyiv.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine received no warning from its partners about Russia's five-missile ballistic strike on Kyiv on 12 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russian drone strikes educational institution in central Rivne, leaving people injured.
A Russian drone struck a building at an educational institution in central Rivne on 13 October, injuring people and causing significant damage to the building.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Ukraine's Air Force comments on delay of air-raid warning in Kyiv.
Yurii Ihnat has stated Ukrainian and allied intelligence will examine why early launch data was missing before Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
At least three people were killed and 37 injured in Kharkiv as Russia launched repeated aerial attacks on the north-eastern Ukrainian city on Monday and overnight. Strikes also caused damage near Lviv, in western Ukraine.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Sudan army chief al-Burhan orders probe into airstrike that killed 72.
Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on Monday ordered a probe into an airstrike that killed 72 people near the Egyptian border. Rights group Emergency Lawyers accused Egypt of carrying out the strike.

[Nile Post] Former ADF recruit and convicted murder suspect Hamza Lyavala has accused former Deputy Chief of Military Intelligence (CMI) Brigadier General Abdul Rugumayo of torturing him and attempting to coerce him into implicating detained General James Birungi in alleged staged bomb attacks in Kampala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Ethiopia: Eritrean Incursions Raise Fears of a Wider Regional War in Ethiopia.

South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Mhona Appoints Board of Inquiry to Probe Lake Kariba Vessel Accident.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Zimbabwe: Mhona Appoints Board of Inquiry to Probe Lake Kariba Vessel Accident.
[263Chat] Transport and Infrastructural Development Minister Felix Mhona has appointed a three-member Board of Inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding a vessel casualty involving the Rural Infrastructural Development Agency (RIDA) on Lake Kariba on August 11, 2026 which killed 97 people.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Namibia: Namibia Appoints First Nuclear Commissioner.
[Namibian] Prime minister Elijah Ngurare has appointed John Titus as Namibia's first nuclear commissioner.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 4 hours ago: South Africa: Police Committee Chairperson Welcomes Sibiya's Departure, Calls for Accountability.
[Parliament of South Africa] The Chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on Police, Mr Ian Cameron, has called on the South African Police Service (SAPS) to investigate any alleged criminal conduct involving Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya and pursue charges where warranted. He warned that Sibiya's departure from the service must not shield him from accountability.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 5 hours ago: South Africa: Soweto Residents Hand Landlords Letters Demanding Foreign Spaza Owners Leave.
[Scrolla] A group calling itself Soweto Uprising 2026 gave Dube landlords letters on Monday demanding that foreign spaza owners leave immediately. Landlord Patricia Mbatha, 70, wants her tenant out but fears community members will attack her, thinking she is protecting him.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: UNDERSTANDING THE NEW AGE OF WAR.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: UNDERSTANDING THE NEW AGE OF WAR.
“And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?” *— William Butler Yeats, The Second Coming* OPENING NOTEWilliam Butler Yeats’ chilling 1920 poem had a backdrop: World War I, the flu pandemic, the Russian Revolution and a sense of impending doom, an inflection point. The gyre is widening and turning again. As wars rage in Eastern Europe, the Middle East and West Asia, it is important to understand what’s happening and why. Questions abound. The answers are not easy to come by, given the unknowns.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Riyadh vows ‘serious’ response amid Houthi escalation.
• Saudi minister says ‘energy security can’t be taken for granted’ • Yemeni rebels warn of ‘swift, painful response’ if US joins war • Iran ‘deeply concerned’, offers to help broker talks • Riyadh airport to remain shut RIYADH: Saudi Arabia vowed a “serious” response after Houthi strikes turned Riyadh’s international airport into a target, killing 18 people in under a week and leaving the world’s biggest oil exporter facing its worst security crisis in more than a decade.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Pakistan condemns Israeli actions in Syria, calls for withdrawal.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has condemned continued Israeli military actions in Syria, calling for Israel’s withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory and full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. Speaking at a UN Security Council briefing on the humanitarian and political situation in Syria on Monday evening, Pakistan’s Acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said Israeli actions violated international law and Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, undermining prospects for regional peace and stability.

Strikes on the airport last week killed at least 18 people

- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Maharashtra man beats wife to death, walks into police station to confess.
In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, a man named Mukesh Kumbhakarna allegedly killed his wife, Rohini, during an argument. The couple had recently returned to Kannad town for the festive season. Following the incident, Kumbhakarna went to the local police station and confessed to the crime. Authorities have registered a murder case against him and an investigation is currently ongoing.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: 3 times cheaper than Patriot? US firm Anduril unveils Steelfin interceptor.
Anduril Industries has unveiled the Steelfin family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles, specifically crafted to meet evolving air defense requirements. These advanced interceptors efficiently neutralize threats such as drones and cruise missiles while maintaining cost-effectiveness. Their modular design allows for tailored configurations across diverse missions, streamlining production. Full-rate manufacturing is anticipated to commence by late 2028 or early 2029 following rigorous testing.

Observers say it is also intended to send a message to Washington and Seoul, serve as a permanent showroom for the North’s arms exports and visibly enshrine its nuclear programme as an irreversible part of state policy.
